title: From Trucks… To $500M Exit
description:
A logistics entrepreneur built a half-billion dollar company without relying on debt—and walked away with it all. The lesson? Cash flow, discipline, and long-term thinking beat flashy leverage.

top_comments.author: @baylordelrosario1465
top_comments.text: My wife and I are not wealthy in terms of millions, but we live our lives based on the same principles of living debt-free. As lifelong educators we made a modest living, but were able to support our 2 children through college, paid off our small home over 10 years ago, fix our own vehicles so no car payments, saved IRA up to nearly $500K, and have modest pensions from our public service careers. We pretty much can do whatever we want (travel to Europe every few years, etc.) and we aren't millionaires...just living within our means and avoiding debt at all costs.

top_comments.author: @AEmery-o3p
top_comments.text:
Do you ever notice that very few of these rich guys speak about the fine financial details of how their journey began.   It’s almost always just a little vague when they speak about the beginning.  

The spark.  It’s ALL about the initial spark.  

I know a guy.  He’s real proud of his millions.   His spark was a phone call from an uncle who had a burger joint in a small town and was willing to do an owner contract with him.   He never talks about that.  He talks about all his “hard work” and ability to “stick to it”.  

Bull shit. 

You had a spark.  What was it?   

Specifically?

Often times these guys literally fall into their spark.  And then yes they do something with it.  


BUT 

THE SPARK.   That wasn’t them.  And they know it.  And the ones who aren’t humble and grounded HATE THAT PART OF THEIR STORY.
